title: My Experience of Trying Our Best in Tracking Expense for a Year
body:
Hi All,
I am providing my household spending breakdown below. I know I have provided this many times before throughout the year. However, it was really insightful for me to see this after tracking spending penny by penny for a year. I am looking for cost-cutting ideas if any. Below average household expenses for last quarter excludes mortgage/rent which is almost fixed and hence not tracked. We are a family of 3 people with 1 primary school going child.
For Apr–Jun 2026 , my average non-rent/mortgage spend was $4,057/month . Overall, we were able to live ok with 1 income.

I’m not using a fixed budget. Instead, I compare my spending against the previous three-month average. If my current spending is below that trend, I consider it a positive result. If it’s above the trend, I investigate the reason and look for ways to reduce it over time.
I’ve already churned as much as possible across electricity, gas, internet, and health insurance. Overall, we managed to reduce our total household expenses over the last quarter so they can now be covered by 1 income. Our goal is to continue reducing expenses gradually without affecting our standard of living, while also increasing our savings and growing our SMSF.
I’m particularly interested in practical suggestions to reduce costs in areas such as:
* Groceries
* Medical and healthcare expenses (e.g. pharmacy costs)
* Utilities outside churning
* Subscriptions (especially in AI subscription costs)
* General household and family spending
